abstract:
Polycrisis Resilience: Human Exposure is a foundational publication within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).
It examines human exposure as a foundational dimension of polycrisis vulnerability, organizes exposure across six interconnected dimensions, distinguishes human exposure, human vulnerability, and Polycrisis Resilience, and establishes seven strategic development pathways to build a world in which fewer people face the conditions that generate systemic vulnerability.

keyFindings.title: Polycrisis Resilience requires transitioning from predominantly reactive crisis management toward the systematic reduction of human exposure to interconnected global risks across environmental, climatic, socioeconomic, health, infrastructural, and institutional dimensions.

Exposure reduction is not identical to vulnerability reduction: a population can remain exposed to a physical hazard while becoming substantially less vulnerable through stronger infrastructure, healthcare, institutions, and adaptive capacity.
Human exposure is highly unequal—low-income economies carry a composite exposure index of 79.0 versus 22.5 in high-income economies, driven by gaps in energy, water, housing, and governance.

Accelerating sustainable development, technological diffusion, economic convergence, environmental improvement, and institutional strengthening compresses global human exposure from 64.0 (2025) to 23.5 by 2050 and 8.5 by 2100 (-86.7%).

contents.title: Executive Summary: Reducing Human Exposure as a Foundation of Polycrisis Resilience
Central H Heuristics Contribution: Exposure, Vulnerability, and Polycrisis Resilience
Six Interconnected Dimensions of Human Exposure
Dimension 1: Environmental Exposure—Air, Water, Heat, and Ecosystem Degradation
Dimension 2: Climate and Physical Exposure—Floods, Droughts, and Sea-Level Rise
Dimension 3: Socioeconomic Exposure—Poverty, Food Insecurity, and Housing
Dimension 4: Health Exposure—Infectious Disease, Malnutrition, and Care Deficits
Dimension 5: Infrastructure and Technological Exposure—Energy, Water, and Digital Gaps
Dimension 6: Conflict and Institutional Exposure—Fragility, Displacement, and Governance
Unequal Distribution of Human Exposure Across Geography and Income
Strategic Pathways 1 & 2: Clean Energy Transitions and Technology Diffusion
Strategic Pathways 3 & 4: Sustainable Convergence and Climate Adaptation
Strategic Pathways 5, 6 & 7: Infrastructure, Human Development, and Institutions
Prevention Economics: Shifting Capital From Crisis Management to Exposure Reduction
Regional Exposure Diagnostics and Global Convergence Priorities
Applied Case Perspectives: Reducing Multi-Dimensional Exposure in Practice
Compounding Exposure, Forced Displacement, and Mobility Resilience
Measuring Human Exposure Reduction: Diagnostics and National Scorecards
Global Policy, Multilateral Finance, and Institutional Reform Agenda
Concluding Synthesis: Building a World With Fewer Exposed Populations
Methodology, Data Architecture, Sensitivity Analysis, and Limitations
